land.text: Sindh, the Soomra realm: 'The Sammas overthrew the Soomras soon after 1335'

predecessors.note: The Soomra dossier ends in 1351 (its infobox) and names this dynasty as successor; Cliopatria's Samma row starts in 1344.

land.text: Sindh, from which Muhammad bin Tughluq's army withdrew after he 'died at Sondha' in 1351

predecessors.note: 'The Sammas then became independent'; the Tughlaq dossier of this batch keeps Sind with Delhi until 1351 and records the loss in that year.

land.text: Sindh, taken by Shah Beg Arghun in the 1520 campaign that 'marked the end of Samma rule in Sindh'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Samma outline to 1525 with no Arghun row; the Arghun dynasty needs a dossier (1520-1554 on its infobox, capital Bukkur).

capitals.name: Samanagar (Thatta)
capitals.note: The page names Samanagar, 'modern Thatta', as the capital and gives no years; the span is the dynasty's. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Thatta.

keyframe_review.note: Holds for 1351 only: the 123,233 km2 (490 cells) outline is the lower Indus, but the Samma page puts the independence in 1351 ('Muhammad bin Tughluq led an expedition against Sindh in 1351 and died at Sondha ... The Sammas then became independent'; infobox start 1351), so 1344-1350 stays with the Tughlaq dossier's Sind. The same page has the Sammas overthrowing the Soomras 'soon after 1335' and a monarchy row from 1336; the choice of 1351 follows both infoboxes (Soomra ends 1351). Sindh's Natural Earth outline is 562 cells; the Samma shape is 0.87 of it.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1344 outline, drawn for 1351 only

keyframe_review.note: 123,201 km2 for 1352-1520: Sindh from the Rann to the Indus bend, which fits 'in Sindh, with parts of Punjab and Balochistan' and 'Multan remained under the Langahs, not the Sammas'. The Kutch, Bhakkar and Gujarat ties the page mentions are not drawn: the Sama Rajput conquest of Kutch is dated only to 'the 14th century' and Bhakkar to a one-year campaign of Nizamuddin II. The page gives no area to compare.

Not Samma land: the Arghun dynasty page has Shah Beg Arghun invade Sindh in 1520 ('In 1520, in the hopes of establishing a new power base, he invaded Sindh'), defeat Jam Feroz, who 'fled to Gujarat', and sack Thatta; that campaign 'marked the end of Samma rule in Sindh'. The Samma page gives 926 AH (1519) for the conquest and its infobox 1524; Cliopatria draws the Samma outline to 1525 with no Arghun row. The outline is right for the land and wrong for the owner from 1520.

correction.text: the same outline, Sindh, as the Arghun dynasty's land from 1520 (a dossier for the Arghuns is needed)

region.text: Sindh, the realm of the Sammas

ledger.note: 1351: the Sammas rule an independent Sindh. Infobox start 1351; 'Muhammad bin Tughluq led an expedition against Sindh in 1351 and died at Sondha, possibly while trying to restore the Soomras. The Sammas then became independent.' The same page has Ibn Battuta recording a Samma rebellion under Jam Tamachi in 1333, the overthrow of the Soomras 'soon after 1335', and Unar's reign as 1336-1339 in one list and 1351-1352 in the table; Cliopatria starts the row in 1344.

region.text: Sindh, from Thatta to the north

ledger.note: 1520: Shah Beg Arghun invades Sindh. 'In 1520, in the hopes of establishing a new power base, he invaded Sindh'; the Samma page puts the conquest in 926 AH (1519) at the battle of Fatehpur.
1520: Jam Feroz is beaten and flees to Gujarat; Thatta is sacked 'during the 1520 campaign'.

1520: Samma rule ends in Sindh. The 1520 campaign 'marked the end of Samma rule in Sindh'; the Arghun infobox begins 'Arghun dynasty begins: 1520'. The Samma page's infobox says 1524 and the table has Feroz ruling to 1524 (another list 1527).

wars.name: Muhammad bin Tughluq's Sindh expedition
wars.outcome: Muhammad died at Sondha in March 1351 pursuing rebels and tax resisters; the Sammas became independent.
wars.note: The Tughlaq page says he was chasing 'rebels and tax resisters in Sindh'; the Samma page adds that he may have been trying to restore the Soomras.

wars.name: Firuz Shah's Thatta campaigns
wars.outcome: Firuz marched in 1362, retreated, and had Thatta's submission and a tribute of 400,000 tankas in 1363 (his page); the Samma page has attacks in 1365 and 1367 'without success' and then Banbhiniyo's surrender, the Sammas 'again subject to Delhi for a time'. No border moved.
wars.note: The two pages disagree on the years; the Tughlaq dossier records the tribute as a vassal event.

wars.name: Arghun raid on Sindh
wars.outcome: 'After 1490, a Mughal army under Shah Beg Arghun raided into Samma territory'; Darya Khan defeated it at Duruh-i-Kureeb and the raiders did not return in Nizamuddin's reign.
wars.note: The page gives no year but 'after 1490'; the span is a bracket.

wars.name: Arghun conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Shah Beg Arghun defeated Jam Feroz, who fled to Gujarat, and sacked Thatta; Samma rule ended.
wars.note: The Samma page dates the conquest 926 AH (1519) at the battle of Fatehpur.

certainty.note: The Indus delta and the Thar frontier are approximate; no page gives a boundary, and Multan (Langahs), Kutch and Bhakkar are the edges the page names.

notes: Sind-Samma Dynasty: three Cliopatria shapes (1344-1525) reviewed against Samma dynasty and Arghun dynasty (two pages, the budget), with the Firuz Shah Tughlaq page cited for the 1363 submission. Dates: start 1351 follows both infoboxes (Samma 1351, Soomra ends 1351) and the page's 'The Sammas then became independent'; Cliopatria's 1344, the page's rebellion of 1333, the overthrow of the Soomras 'soon after 1335' and the monarchy row 1336 are earlier signs of Samma power; a gap-filler may prefer 1336. End 1520 follows the Arghun page; the Samma page says 1519 (926 AH) in the text and 1524 in the infobox, and Cliopatria 1525. Rulers are not given: the Samma page's lists disagree (Unar 1336-1339 or 1351-1352; Feroz to 1524 or 1527). Needs a dossier: arghun-dynasty (Shah Beg Arghun, 1520-1554, Bukkur; Cliopatria has no Arghun row, and the Samma outline of 1521-1525 is theirs). The Langah Sultanate (Multan) has a dossier already. Vassal status under Delhi in 1363 is recorded by the suzerain (tughlaq-dynasty, vassal_start 1363). Region names: none missing.
